newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power extends gains on cold, outages.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power extends gains on cold, outages.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly higher Wednesday due to cooler temperatures in the region and the absence of some nuclear power, sources said.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to hover about two to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal through Friday but then return to near-normal levels by early next week.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Thursday rose gradually throughout today's session, with deals reported done anywhere from $25.50 to $32.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Traders said most deals were done in the $28.00-29.50 range, as compared with Tuesday's $26.00-28.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were talked at $14.50-16.00 per MWh, but no deals were confirmed done.
TVA was not offering power as its 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power unit, in Spring City, Tenn., remained off line after shutting down late Monday.
In its morning status report, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said the unit is expected to restart Thursday, but the company would not comment.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Thursday delivery climbed into the $24.00-26.00 per MWh range, as compared with Tuesday's range of $22.50-23.50.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was assessed at $14.00-15.00 per MWh.
Propping up power prices at the border was news that Georgia Power's 741 MW Hatch 1 nuclear power unit was shut down. The company said it expects to return the unit to the grid Sunday or Monday.
In Florida, firm, peak prices on a 16-hour schedule were talked $2-3 higher around $24.00.

Separately, Virginia Power said it postponed the restart of its 781 MW Surry 1 nuclear power unit until early Saturday. The unit, shut last Friday due to a steam pipe leak, was previously expected to return to the grid this morning.
Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, will also not restart as scheduled. The company said the unit will likely restart this weekend.
Oconee units 1 and 3, shut since October and each generating 846 MW, are expected to restart in February.
All three units are in Seneca, S.C.

Also, Florida Power and Light's 860 MW Crystal River 3 nuclear unit, shut since early September, has been added to the NRC's watchlist. The company said the unit would not restart until the fourth quarter of 1997.
